title: Low-two supersets lattice conjecture
formal: For every coinfinite c.e. low-two set A⊆N, is L*(A) isomorphic to E* as a bounded lattice?
definitions:
A set A of natural numbers is computably enumerable (c.e.) if a finite ordinary Turing program enumerates exactly A. Write A≤_T B when an oracle Turing machine with membership access to B decides membership in A on every input. Equivalence under mutual reducibility defines a Turing degree. R is the set of degrees containing a c.e. set, ordered by ≤_T; it is not the set of all degrees below the halting problem. All quantification over degrees below is over R. The language has only ≤ and logical equality, with no named degrees or parameters unless explicitly stated.

For a set X, its jump X′ is the halting set {e: the e-th oracle program with oracle X halts on input e}, for a fixed effective enumeration of programs. Define X^(0)=X and X^(k+1)=(X^(k))′. Low-n means X^(n) is Turing equivalent to the n-th jump of the empty set. Coinfinite means N\A is infinite. For sets X,Y write X=*Y if their symmetric difference is finite, and X⊆*Y if X\Y is finite. E* consists of all c.e. sets modulo =*, ordered by ⊆*, with union as join, intersection as meet, bottom [∅] and top [N]. L*(A) is the sublattice of classes represented by c.e. X⊇A, with bottom [A] and top [N]. An isomorphism is an arbitrary bijection preserving both lattice operations and bounds. No effective presentation of the quotient or computability of the isomorphism is assumed.

import_provenance.original_statement: For every coinfinite computably enumerable low₂ set A, is the lattice of its computably enumerable supersets modulo finite difference isomorphic to the entire lattice of computably enumerable sets modulo finite difference? Here low₂ means A″ has the same Turing degree as the double jump of the computable sets.
